messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 4187659999 - decode-node kernel OOM detected on streamers-prod-03. Paging oncall: @alice (oncall). Auto-eviction started. > severity: P1.

alice (oncall): got it. seeing repeated CUDA OOMs on streamers-prod-03 during decode loop. spikes coincide with long streaming sessions.

alice (oncall): quick status: node has 4/8 decoders unhealthy. kernel logs show `CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN` followed by `out of memory`. memory usage climbs steadily before crash.

raj (runtime): thanks. can you dump last 30s of logs + tail of decode runtime? i'll check kv-cache growth.

alice (oncall): pasting clipped logs: ```
E 03:14:21 decode.cu:456 kernel_launch failed: CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN
E 03:14:21 decode.cu:460 attempted alloc 1.2G, avail 900M
I 03:14:22 session_mgr: streaming session id=usr-xx token_count=14200
I 03:14:23 batching: appended 40 requests (avg len 1200)
```

maya (infra): mount metrics: host memory + GPU memory trending up on that box. eviction triggered but node didn't drain in time. container restarted twice in last 7m.

tom (cs): flagged: a small set of customers saw `500` and truncated streams. ticket #INC-1199 from Acme reported partial responses and reconnect loops.

alice (oncall): immediate mitigation proposals: 1) temporarily disable long-streaming sessions by rejecting requests with `client_max_tokens>2000`; 2) apply an ingress token cap header sanitizer; 3) restart node after eviction. which do we want first?

li (oncall-lead): do 1 + 2 now. minimal blast radius. make sure to annotate which route rules. then restart node.

raj (runtime): working on a quick router filter. patch below: ```diff
+ if (req.headers['x-client-max-tokens'] && parseInt(...) > 2000) {
+   return 400 'token_cap_exceeded';
+ }
```

alice (oncall): applied a temporary nginx route rule to reject based on header `x-client-max-tokens`. also pushed a rate-limit knob to 5 concurrent streaming sessions per user-id.

deploy-bot: deploy started: routing/filter-hotfix v1 -> prod (canary 5%) by maya.

maya (infra): canary landed on 2 nodes including streamers-prod-03. watching memory.

alice (oncall): node restarted gracefully at 03:22:10. errors dropping. GPU memory plateaued.

tom (cs): updated Acme: we pushed a temporary safeguard to limit long streams; working on full root-cause. they saw 14% of streaming calls drop during the window.

raj (runtime): early hypothesis: kv-cache not evicting correctly for a subset of sessions where client-supplied max_tokens is misinterpreted (string v number), causing unbounded accumulation. also batching policy allowed huge batches of long sequences.

alice (oncall): i grabbed request-ids from logs: r_3a4f1c..r_3a4f9c. will attach to post-incident impact doc.

raj (runtime): i'll add guardrails in runtime: ensure `max_tokens` parsed as int, enforce hard ceiling at 4000 at the codec layer, and cap batch cumulative token length. pushing a non-breaking config change as hotfix (no model binary change).

maya (infra): telemetry: cluster-level token histogram shows a 0.6% tail > 10k tokens during the incident. that explains pressure.

alice (oncall): continuing: suggest we keep the header sanitizer for 60m while runtime change deploys. any objections?

li (oncall-lead): go ahead. also open a rollback plan in case downstream breaks (clients expecting large batches).

raj (runtime): hotfix PR: `runtime:strict-max-tokens-parse` created and deployed to canary. changes: safe-parse, hard-cap 4000 tokens, and batch-shaping to split oversized requests.

deploy-bot: canary deploy success: runtime-hotfix v2 -> 3 nodes. monitoring 10m.

alice (oncall): after hotfix, streamers-prod-03 stable for 8m. no new OOMs. decoder restarts stopped.

tom (cs): running impact summary: ~1.2k requests affected in 12m window, ~80 unique customers, highest impact on 3 accounts (Acme, BetaApps, Shoply). CS sending targeted followups.

raj (runtime): follow-up engineering actions: - add unit tests for token header parsing; - add integrated test for large-batch shaping; - add backpressure metric to detect cumulative batch token size; - implement auto-evict threshold earlier in request life-cycle.

maya (infra): infra actions: - mark streamers-prod-03 as degraded until full postmortem; - add node-level OOM alert with 3-restart suppression to avoid noise; - check driver versions and CUDA telemetry across fleet.

alice (oncall): incident severity reduced to P3 at 03:40 after mitigation holding. keeping thread open for postmortem notes.

li (oncall-lead): good. we should prepare a customer-facing blameless summary and include the temporary mitigations + ETA for runtime fix in next 48h. assign owners.

tom (cs): will draft customer note and share.

raj (runtime): i'll own runtime fix rollout and tests. estimate full rollout in 6h with coordinated QA.

maya (infra): i'll run fleet-wide driver health check and schedule maintenance if mismatch found.

alice (oncall): closing immediate pager; leaving sandbox notes and logs at https://redwood.internal/err/4187659999 (redacted). tagging auditors. if anyone sees new OOMs, ping this thread. :handshake:

deploy-bot: post-incident checklist created: INC-4187659999. Actions assigned.

alice (oncall): thanks team. follow-ups: postmortem owner: raj; customer comms owner: tom; infra follow-up: maya.

li (oncall-lead): great work. moving to incident retrospective channel shortly.

raj (runtime): quick note: added temporary metric `ingress.total_token_length` to tracing. will alert on 95p > 8k.

tom (cs): ticket updates sent. customers acknowledged mitigation. will track any regressions.

alice (oncall): thread archived at 03:46.
